政.meaning: Two mayors argue in the town square, each flapping a giant <part>fan</part> and shouting that they alone are <part>correct</part>. The crowd takes sides, the fans flap harder, and nothing gets done. Welcome to <kanji>politics</kanji>.
政.on: Whoever wins gets the key to the town <sound>sa</sound>fe.
政.kun: A lla<sound>ma</sound> joins the race, sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and promises a coral <sound>ree</sound>f to every <sound>go</sound>pher in town and a <sound>to</sound>tem pole for every park.

曇.meaning: The <part>sun</part> is sunbathing, when a fat grey <part>cloud</part> plops down on top of it like a cat on a warm laptop. Shadows spread, the picnic blankets are packed up, and the light goes dull. The sky starts to <kanji>cloud up</kanji>.
曇.on: A <sound>don</sound>key at the picnic grumbles, then eats all the sandwiches left behind.
曇.kun: A <sound>coo</sound>k shoos a <sound>mo</sound>le off the cake as the sky turns grey.

露.meaning: A snail wakes to find the garden <part>path</part> sparkling, though no <part>rain</part> fell overnight. Every blade of grass along it wears tiny glass beads. The snail slurps one up for breakfast: fresh <kanji>dew</kanji>.
露.on: A <sound>ro</sound>dent scurries along behind it, leaving tiny wet footprints.
露.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' the snail sneezes, splashing a drop onto a <sound>yu</sound>zu lying in the grass.

濯.meaning: A <part>peacock</part> opens a launderette. Customers drop off their socks, and it swishes them through <part>water drops</part> with its huge tail, then fans them dry. Clean and folded in an hour: the best <kanji>laundry</kanji> in town.
濯.on: It gets paid in food: one crunchy <sound>ta</sound>co per bag.
濯.kun: A <sound>su</sound>shi chef brings his apron, and another <sound>su</sound>shi chef brings his: the peacock rinses both.

犬.meaning: A <part>large</part> man spreads his arms wide for a hug, and a muddy <part>dot</part> lands on his shoulder: a paw print. Something has jumped up to lick his ear and is wagging all over him. It's a <kanji>dog</kanji>.
犬.on: It drags him back to its <sound>ken</sound>nel to share its blanket.
犬.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' he squeals, as it pushes him into a cosy <sound>noo</sound>k at the back.

献.meaning: Every summer a <part>dog</part> trots up from the <part>south</part> with a basket of warm figs in its mouth and lays it at the door of an old hermit's cave. It never asks for anything back. It's an <kanji>offering</kanji>.
献.on: The hermit builds it a <sound>ken</sound>nel out of the empty fig baskets.
献.kun: Next year it brings a <sound>ta</sound>co, a <sound>te</sound>nt and a lla<sound>ma</sound>, and lays them down with a sneeze: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'

状.meaning: A <part>dog</part> sits at the foot of a <part>climbing pole</part>, where it has sat for three years, refusing to move. Nobody changes anything: same dog, same pole, same spot every day. That's the <kanji>status quo</kanji>.
状.on: A <sound>jo</sound>ey peeks out of its mother's pouch, sees the dog and decides not to bother either.

症.meaning: In a <part>leaky shed</part> clinic, a doctor runs down her list and every guess is <part>correct</part>: runny nose, sneezing, hot forehead. A drip from the roof lands on the patient's head. Yes, it's a cold: you've got all the <kanji>symptoms</kanji>.
症.on: To cheer him up, she puts on a puppet <sound>show</sound> with two tissues.
